summary.headline: YES Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 33.7% YoY to INR 1,071 crore, with NII up 17.5% and cost-to-income down to 62.8%.
summary.overview: Net profit grew 33.7% YoY to INR 1,071 crore and operating profit rose 25.5% to INR 1,704 crore, even with lower Security Receipts gains (INR 86 crore vs INR 338 crore) and lower treasury income. Reported gross slippages fell to 1.4% from 1.6% QoQ and 2.4% YoY, with retail slippages at a 10-quarter low. Advances grew 18.3% YoY to INR 2.85 lakh crore, with management stating underlying average-balance growth of 15-16%. Management reiterated its aim of a full-year ROA around 1% and a NIM above 3% over the next two years, and a board enabling resolution for capital raising was flagged.

segments.name: Corporate and Institutional Banking
segments.commentary: Grew strongly in advances; management said part of the growth is transitional and shorter-tenure in nature.

segments.name: Commercial Banking (largely MSME)
segments.commentary: Advances grew 17% YoY; management said the portfolio quality remains high with controlled Q1 slippages.

segments.name: Retail Banking
segments.commentary: Advances grew only 6.9% YoY, but retail disbursements grew 27.5% YoY; retail slippages were at a 10-quarter low.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 ROA: aspiration around 1%; management expects core ROA to expand 15-20 bps in FY27, with the reported 1% ROA dependent on resolutions and bond/trading gains.
NIM: near-term aim of 3%+ over the next 2 years; management later said north of 3% is achievable in FY28, with expansion described as a steady climb rather than quarter-to-quarter.
Advances growth targeted at 15-17%, a little above industry; underlying average-balance loan growth of 15-16%.
SR recoveries: guidance of INR 800-1,000 crore for FY27 maintained, dependent on J.C. Flower's execution.
Capital: 14% CET-1 seen as sufficient for about the next 4 quarters of growth; enabling approval for capital raise remains in place until the AGM. Future raise would be targeted in the 13% handle.
Retail: management expects double-digit retail book growth in about 3-4 quarters; mid-teens loan growth is the stated goal.

financial_highlights.value: INR 564 crore incl. INR 86 crore from SR portfolio

qa_highlights.question: What net advances target do you have for the year, and is the board capital-raise resolution a signal of need?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances growth is targeted at about 15-17%, a little above industry. Capital resolution is an enabler to stay ready; 3-4 quarters of growth cushion is available for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the FCNR(B) deposit and leverage product progressing and what constrains it?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is strong and leverage limits are being filled, capped at 9x for now. Pace is slowed by higher overseas borrowing spreads and uneven global liquidity; limits are being set up with international banks including SMBC.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins improve and what is the FY28 view?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are runoff of low-yield RIDF and priority-sector deposits, deposit repricing and CASA mix. Management said north of 3% NIM is achievable in FY28, with a steady climb rather than quarter-to-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SR recoveries fall QoQ and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 SR redemption was INR 86 crore versus about INR 450 crore in Q4. SR face value outstanding is INR 1,500 crore with NAV above INR 2,000 crore; FY27 guidance of INR 800-1,000 crore is maintained but depends on J.C. Flower execution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital-raise timeline and does the AT1 court case link to it?
qa_highlights.answer: The approval is an annual enabling resolution, valid till the AGM and not tied to the court case. CET-1 of 14% is seen as enough for about 4 quarters; any raise would target the 13% handle. No provision has been made for the court case.

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail growth plan and how will disbursements translate into book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail book is flat to 7% growth due to run-off; disbursements grow 25-30% and book growth should follow in about 3-4 quarters. Secured mix of about 75% is the guardrail, with LAP, personal loans and franchise products.

qa_highlights.question: Did MSME slippages rise and is there West Asia war exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Commercial Banking slippages were controlled in Q1, with limited impact from the West Asia conflict and portfolio quality remaining high.

capex_capacity: No capex or capacity-expansion plans discussed; this is a bank, so the capital discussion is the relevant equivalent.

Capital: CET-1 at 14%, which management said is sufficient for about the next 4 quarters of growth (CFO also cited at least one year). Board enabling resolution for capital raise is an enabler kept in place until the AGM; future raise to be targeted in the 13% handle, versus prior raise at about 11-11.5% CET-1.

DTA benefit cited: bank can grow at 12-13% RWA without consuming capital; ROE of about 8-8.5% accretes to capital. Growth of 15-16% would consume more capital but management said it is still manageable.

ECL transition: no public estimate yet; management expects gross ECL impact not to be very material and, with new credit RWA norms from 1 April, not material to core equity. Numbers to be firmed up during the year.

Liquidity and funding: LCR 138.2%; FCNR(B) leverage limits filled, with leverage capped at 9x for now; limits being set up with international banks including SMBC, with spreads and global liquidity slowing pace.
demand_pricing: Advances up 18.3% YoY to INR 2.85 lakh crore; management said underlying average-balance growth is 15-16% and the target is 15-17%, a little above industry.
Corporate and Institutional Banking grew strongly, with part of the growth transitional and shorter-tenure; Commercial Banking (largely MSME) grew 17% YoY; Retail advances grew 6.9% YoY.
Retail disbursements grew 27.5% YoY; management said fresh retail momentum is 25-30% and double-digit book growth is expected in about 3-4 quarters; mid-teens loan growth is the stated goal.
Deposits up 14.3% YoY to INR 3.15 lakh crore; CASA up 14.3% YoY (15% on average balance). Retail and branch-led deposits are close to 60% of total. Average-balance CD ratio unchanged QoQ.
NIM 2.7%, up 20 bps YoY and stable QoQ; cost of deposits down since April 2025 without attrition; management said NIM north of 3% is achievable in FY28, with a steady climb rather than linear.
Core fees up 18.7% YoY across cards, third-party products, forex and transaction banking. Cost-to-income 62.8% vs 67.1% a year ago.
Competition: deposit competition described as intense with the rate cut cycle now on par. FCNR(B) demand strong, with a stated leverage cap of 9x.
risks_watch: SR recoveries are lumpy and depend on J.C. Flower execution; Q1 recoveries of INR 86 crore fall well short of the INR 800-1,000 crore FY27 run-rate needed.
Margin path: NIM is 2.7%, with deposit competition intense and the rate-cut cycle now on par; management cautioned that expansion will be a steady climb.
Growth mix: much of the 18.3% advances growth is transitional, shorter-tenure corporate lending, while retail book growth is only 6.9%.
Dilution: capital raise enabler in place; any raise would be targeted in the 13% CET-1 handle, and the quantum and timing are unspecified.
ECL transition impact and the new credit RWA norms from 1 April are not yet quantified; management said it will update during the year.
FCNR(B) leverage growth depends on overseas bank limits; the 9x cap and pace of limit setup are unresolved.
key_quotes: Our Net Profit grew 33.7% that is year-on-year to INR 1,071 crores.
I would caution that, with the rate cut cycle now on par and Deposit competition intense, margin expansion will be a steady structural climb rather than a straight-line quarter-to-quarter.
So it is not a trigger of any particular event or court case.
We will raise it, let's say, in the 13% handle.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, asset quality and fee momentum, but cautious on near-term margin expansion (steady climb, not linear), retail book growth (3-4 quarters out) and SR recovery timing, which management repeatedly said depends on J.C. Flower.

growth.why: Management guides full-year FY27 advances growth of 15-17% (underlying average-balance growth 15-16%, retail disbursements +27.5% YoY) and core ROA expansion of 15-20 bps, with SR gains of INR 800-1,000 crore held; backing is demand-led and partial, with no capacity additions, and the capital headroom (CET-1 14%) is described as sufficient for about 4 quarters of growth.
